tasks.short: Produce the HR dashboard pack and answer managers’ reporting questions.

today.trigger: The daily refresh finishes, a management meeting approaches, or a manager requests a different breakdown.
steps: Check the nightly AFAS extract and obtain missing recruitment or training exports.
Reconcile headcount, hiring, onboarding, retention and absence measures.
Adjust Power BI filters or Excel tables for the requested audience.
Explain changes, check sensitive breakdowns and share the report.
drudgery: Rebuilding the same site and period comparisons
today.time_sinks: Repeated reconciliation, custom cuts and formatting consume time even when the underlying question is unchanged.

lenses.faster: Calculate approved measures once and generate standard site comparisons and variance notes automatically. Repeated exports, formatting and arithmetic disappear.
lenses.autonomous: After a validated refresh, regenerate approved reports and release them to existing authorised audiences. Failed checks stop publication and create an exception.
lenses.ambitious: Follow every hiring cohort through day 90, showing where vacancies fail to become productive, retained hires. Show pending outcomes separately so recent hires do not distort results.
lenses.joy: Remove pack assembly and repeated reconciliation. Spend the recovered time explaining what site managers can improve.
lenses.options: Offer consistent views by site, role family, shift category and hiring source, subject to disclosure controls. Compare alternative explanations before recommending an intervention.
lenses.altitude: Own the metric definitions, quality checks and reporting service instead of assembling each report.
reach: Recruiter reporting on funnel delays and offer acceptance
L&D reporting on week-one onboarding and certificate completion
Controller reconciliation of workforce counts and labour costs

tasks.human_edge: Agree what productive means for warehouse, transport and office roles, and distinguish a useful operational explanation from a misleading correlation.
tasks.pattern_why: Approved calculations, filters and report layouts can run as ordinary software. AI can help build them; routine production needs no model.

in_practice.trigger: The nightly extract and required supplementary feeds pass freshness and reconciliation checks.
steps: Load approved fields and reconcile source totals, employee identifiers and reporting dates.
Calculate versioned metrics, separating employees from agency workers and mature from pending 90-day cohorts.
Apply audience permissions and agreed small-group disclosure rules.
Generate standard reports with source timestamps and rule-based variance notes.
Release approved outputs; route failed checks and new reporting requests to the analyst.
in_practice.human_gate: Approve new measures, audiences and report templates before activation; review exceptions and sensitive custom analyses.
systems: Recruitee and Studytube approved exports or validated integrations
Proposed scheduled validation job in an IT-approved runtime
data_needed: Vacancy, offer, hire and start dates with an approved cross-system identifier
Agreed productivity milestone recorded by the responsible manager
Metric definitions, access matrix and disclosure rules
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint reporting register containing run ID, source dates, metric version, checks and publication links.

evidence.claim: AFAS provides GetConnectors for retrieving Profit data; the required fields and permissions still need verification.
Power BI supports scheduled refresh, providing an existing foundation for recurring reporting.
The proposed workflow, 75% human-time saving and 3-times processing speedup are planning estimates, not measured Noordhaven results.

risks: Productivity is not supplied by the listed systems unless managers record an agreed milestone.
Unfilled roles, multiple-position vacancies and hires without 90 days of follow-up can produce misleading North Star denominators.
Small site or role groups can reveal individuals even when names are removed.
Nightly source refresh remains the freshness limit; faster report production does not create live data.
research_questions: Can approved identifiers reliably join Recruitee hires, AFAS employees and Studytube learners?
What numerator, denominator, observation window and productivity milestone define the North Star?
How much of the 160.8 hours is repeatable production rather than new analysis?
Can the automated pack reproduce three historical reporting periods within agreed tolerances?

tasks.short: Get current HR information to the right managers before they need it.

today.trigger: A report is due, a manager asks for information, or a refresh problem threatens a deadline.
steps: Check whether the relevant data and reports are current.
Identify the audience and confirm their access.
Send report links and explain availability or limitations.
Chase missing inputs, failed deliveries and unresolved access requests.
drudgery: Answering repeated questions about which version is current
today.time_sinks: Manual status checks and recipient maintenance create interruptions across the working day.

lenses.faster: Maintain one report catalogue with owners, audiences, deadlines and refresh status. Replace individual reminders with scheduled, permission-aware links.
lenses.autonomous: Successful validated refreshes release routine updates; missed deadlines trigger an alert to the report owner. Changed access remains subject to approval.
lenses.ambitious: Provide a dependable information service for all three sites, including clear data cut-offs for shift managers. Measure whether information arrived before the decision it supports.
lenses.joy: Remove the daily work of chasing updates and resending links. Keep the conversations about what managers need to know.
lenses.options: Offer a daily operational view, weekly site briefing and monthly executive pack from the same definitions. Let managers choose an appropriate approved cadence.
lenses.altitude: Design information delivery standards and exception handling instead of acting as the distribution desk.
reach: HR Administrator coordination of recurring reporting deadlines
HRBP distribution of site management briefings
Controller coordination of workforce reporting cut-offs

tasks.human_edge: Judge when a technically correct update needs explanation, a private conversation or a delay because it could mislead its audience.
tasks.pattern_why: Freshness checks, deadlines, audience rules and delivery retries are explicit rules. A model adds little to routine routing.

in_practice.trigger: A validated report becomes available or a delivery deadline is missed.
steps: Read refresh status, quality results and the approved delivery schedule.
Check the configured audience against current access permissions.
Release a timestamped report link through the approved channel.
Record dispatch status and retry eligible technical failures without duplicating messages.
Escalate stale data, invalid audiences and missed deadlines to the named owner.
in_practice.human_gate: Approve initial audiences, cadence and access changes; intervene for sensitive communications and unresolved failures.
systems: Proposed workflow automation, subject to tenant and licence checks
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint delivery register with report version, audience group, dispatch result and escalation status.

evidence.claim: Power BI subscriptions can send after the first scheduled refresh of the day; this does not provide every-refresh delivery or a custom quality gate.
A separate rules-based workflow could add validation gates, escalation and controlled link delivery.
The 65% human-time saving and 2.5-times delivery-workflow speedup are untested estimates.

risks: A successful technical refresh can still contain incomplete business data.
Email attachments and previews can expose information outside the intended report access controls.
Dispatch success does not prove that a manager read or understood the report.
Too many alerts can obscure the few requiring action.
research_questions: Which information has a genuine operational deadline for each site and shift?
Do current Power BI licences and tenant settings support the required delivery routes?
Can access changes be reflected before the next distribution?
What proportion of current requests concerns delivery rather than interpretation?

tasks.short: Keep HR data feeds, measures and dashboards working when source systems change.

today.trigger: A refresh fails, a source field changes, or HR needs a revised measure.
steps: Inspect refresh errors and compare source extracts with expected structures.
Trace the affected joins, transformations, measures and visuals.
Modify queries, calculations or mappings.
Reconcile results and test access restrictions.
Publish the change and update documentation.
drudgery: Tracing renamed fields through several reports
today.time_sinks: Finding dependencies and proving that a small repair has not changed unrelated HR figures.

lenses.faster: Use a coding assistant to trace dependencies, propose repairs and draft meaningful regression checks. Keep source schemas and metric definitions available as context.
lenses.autonomous: Run freshness, schema and reconciliation checks after each load. Automatically prepare an incident and proposed repair when a known failure occurs.
lenses.ambitious: Give every important HR measure an owner, documented lineage and a historical reconciliation check. Detect breakage before managers encounter it.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive debugging and documentation work. Keep the satisfying work of improving reliability and simplifying the model.
lenses.options: Compare a narrow repair, a reusable mapping change and a broader model simplification before choosing.
lenses.altitude: Own the reliability and change process for HR information rather than patching individual dashboards.
reach: Controller maintenance of shared workforce cost mappings
HR Administrator ownership of recurring data-quality exception lists
L&D maintenance of certificate-reporting mappings

tasks.human_edge: Recognise when an apparent technical repair changes a CAO-related definition, historical comparison or access boundary.
tasks.pattern_why: Diagnosis spans logs, schemas, code and tests. An agent can prepare a complete repair, but the analyst must approve production changes.

in_practice.trigger: A scheduled check fails or an approved change request enters the maintenance queue.
steps: Collect sanitised error logs, schema differences and affected report dependencies.
Have an approved coding agent propose a patch in an isolated development copy.
Run reconciliation, historical-period and audience-access tests.
Present the patch, test results, changed definitions and rollback instructions.
After approval, deploy through controlled credentials and verify the next refresh.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves every production patch; the relevant business owner also approves changed definitions or access rules.
systems: Power BI development and production workspaces, if provisioned
Proposed version-controlled query and model repository
data_needed: Expected totals and historical test periods
in_practice.logs_to: Proposed version-controlled change history and restricted SharePoint release register, including approval and rollback references.

evidence.claim: Microsoft documents that source schema changes can break visuals, measures, relationships and security expressions.
An agent could assemble proposed repairs and test evidence from controlled technical inputs; Noordhaven's environment has not been assessed.
The 40% human-time saving and 1.6-times repair speedup are planning estimates.

risks: A plausible repair can silently change denominators or duplicate employee records.
Tests can preserve an existing error if their expected values are not independently reconciled.
Giving an agent production credentials could allow unintended changes or data exposure.
One analyst remains a maintenance bottleneck without IT backup and a usable runbook.
research_questions: Are query definitions, source schemas and deployment history available in a form an agent can inspect?
Can development be isolated from production with synthetic or minimised data?
Which incidents are repetitive, and which require a business-definition decision?
Can proposed repairs pass independent reconciliations and access tests on historical failures?

tasks.short: Help managers understand or fix problems with HR reports and dashboards.

today.trigger: A manager reports a wrong figure, missing access, a broken visual or uncertainty about a measure.
steps: Ask for the report, filters, timestamp and expected result.
Reproduce the issue and distinguish access, data and interpretation problems.
Check the relevant measure, refresh history and source records.
Explain the answer or route the repair and access request.
Record the resolution for future questions.
drudgery: Requesting the same missing diagnostic details
Repeating explanations of filters and definitions
Searching old messages for earlier resolutions
today.time_sinks: Back-and-forth messages and context switching often take longer than the eventual fix.

lenses.faster: Use a structured request form and draft answers from approved definitions and resolved incidents. Collect report IDs and filter details before the analyst investigates.
lenses.autonomous: Classify new requests and retrieve relevant guidance automatically. Deterministic instructions can answer simple navigation questions; substantive AI answers remain reviewed.
lenses.ambitious: Make support usable for shift managers with short, role-appropriate guidance. Use recurring questions to improve reports and definitions.
lenses.joy: Remove repeated clarification and searching through message history. Keep the work of solving unfamiliar problems and helping managers use evidence well.
lenses.options: Offer a short explanation, a worked example or a guided troubleshooting path depending on the question.
lenses.altitude: Design a support service that prevents recurring confusion instead of answering every question from scratch.
reach: HR Administrator support for locating approved HR reports
HRBP preparation of explanations for site managers
L&D creation of short dashboard guidance

tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a technical question conceals concern about trust, fairness or how a manager's team is being represented.
tasks.pattern_why: A model can turn an unstructured request into a structured ticket and draft a sourced answer inside a controlled support process.

in_practice.trigger: A user submits an HR reporting support request.
steps: Collect report ID, filters, timestamp and a description without unnecessary employee details.
Classify the request and retrieve guidance the requester is authorised to access.
Draft an answer with source links, or identify missing evidence and the correct escalation owner.
Have the analyst verify substantive answers and send the response.
Record the approved resolution and propose a knowledge-base update.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst checks substantive AI responses and all proposed repairs; authorised owners approve access changes.
systems: Teams or an approved Microsoft 365 request form
data_needed: Approved metric dictionary and user guidance
Requester's permitted audience and report access
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint support list containing request category, cited guidance, reviewed answer and resolution status.

evidence.claim: Microsoft publishes troubleshooting guidance for refresh failures that can support a curated support knowledge base.
Retrieval-supported ticket classification and answer drafting are plausible language-model uses, but this particular support service is proposed.
The 45% human-time saving and 1.7-times resolution speedup are untested estimates.

risks: An answer can sound authoritative while citing an outdated definition.
Screenshots and support messages can contain salary, absence or other personal information.
Retrieved documents and user messages must be treated as content, not instructions to change permissions or execute actions.
Automating intake will not shorten delays caused by unavailable source owners.
research_questions: What share of recent support requests could approved guidance resolve?
Can retrieval enforce the requester's existing permissions?
Does a trial reduce clarification messages without increasing incorrect answers?
Which requests should always go directly to the analyst or IT?

tasks.short: Track which HR reporting users are served and where new reporting needs are emerging.

today.trigger: Assuming 'customers' means internal users of HR analytics, review demand when teams change or reporting requests accumulate.
steps: List current report audiences, owners and site contacts.
Review approved report-usage summaries and incoming requests.
Compare coverage with vacancies, hiring volumes and organisational changes.
Discuss unmet needs with HRBPs and site managers.
Prioritise additions to the reporting backlog.
drudgery: Checking whether reports have an active audience
today.time_sinks: Combining usage, requests and organisational changes to identify underserved teams.

lenses.faster: Join approved audience, usage and request summaries into a reporting-coverage view. Replace manual stakeholder-list comparisons.
lenses.autonomous: Refresh a list of teams with changing demand, missing report ownership or unresolved requests. Keep outreach and prioritisation with the analyst.
lenses.ambitious: Check whether all three sites and shift-management groups receive useful information, including groups that rarely request it themselves.
lenses.joy: Remove list maintenance and usage counting. Keep discovery conversations and the work of making reports useful.
lenses.options: Compare demand by operational importance, number of users served and connection to productive 90-day hires.
lenses.altitude: Manage the portfolio of HR information services instead of responding only to the loudest requester.
reach: HRBP collection of site reporting needs
HR Director preparation of HR service priorities
L&D identification of dashboard training needs

tasks.human_edge: Understand why a team does not use a report; low usage can reflect unsuitable access, shift patterns or a poor report rather than lack of need.
tasks.pattern_why: Coverage checks and demand indicators can be calculated from structured registers. The internal-customer interpretation needs confirmation before implementation.

in_practice.trigger: The weekly usage summary, request register or organisational mapping changes.
steps: Read approved team-level usage, report ownership and request summaries.
Map existing coverage to sites, functions and relevant management groups.
Flag coverage gaps using agreed demand indicators and thresholds.
Produce a prioritised review list with the reason behind each flag.
Record the analyst's decision after discussion with the relevant HRBP.
in_practice.human_gate: Approve the meaning of 'customer', permitted usage analysis and thresholds initially; the analyst decides priorities and any outreach.
systems: Power BI usage metrics, if enabled and licensed
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint reporting-demand register with rule version, supporting indicators and prioritisation decisions.

evidence.claim: Power BI provides report-usage metrics, subject to permissions, tenant settings and licensing.
The SER explains OR consent rights concerning employee-data arrangements; usage monitoring needs an assessment of the applicable arrangement.
The internal-customer mapping, 55% human-time saving and 1.8-times speedup are hypothetical.

risks: The original O*NET task may concern external commercial customers; that would need different ownership and data absent from this brief.
Individual usage monitoring could become employee surveillance; use approved aggregate measures and assess AVG and OR requirements.
Report views are an imperfect measure of usefulness.
Office users may dominate recorded demand while shift managers remain underserved.
research_questions: Does Noordhaven actually perform this task for internal reporting customers, or is the O*NET mapping unsuitable?
Can team-level demand be measured without retaining individual usage histories?
Do HRBPs recognise the flagged coverage gaps as real needs?
Would the proposed review change reporting priorities enough to justify maintaining it?

tasks.short: Build HR dashboards and data models that connect recruitment, onboarding and employee outcomes.

today.trigger: HR needs a new dashboard, joined dataset or spreadsheet tool.
steps: Clarify the decision, audience and required measures.
Inspect source exports, identifiers and available history.
Design joins, calculations, access rules and outputs.
Build the first version and reconcile sample cases.
Review with users, publish and document ownership.
today.time_sinks: Source discovery, identity matching and agreeing definitions usually take longer than drawing the dashboard.

lenses.faster: Generate a first model, measures and interface from an agreed specification using synthetic data. Reuse approved joins and access patterns.
lenses.autonomous: An approved request can trigger a development draft and test results. Production release still requires review of meaning, access and maintainability.
lenses.ambitious: Build a reusable hire-to-day-90 dataset rather than another isolated dashboard. Let HR test whether onboarding improvements accompany better retained, productive hiring outcomes.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive code and spreadsheet scaffolding. Keep problem framing, user discovery and choosing useful measures.
lenses.options: Produce several layouts and compare simple cohort comparisons with more detailed funnel views before building the final output.
lenses.altitude: Design reusable HR data products and development standards instead of constructing every tool separately.
reach: Recruiter creation of hiring funnel tools
L&D creation of onboarding and certificate dashboards
FP&A preparation of workforce planning scenarios

tasks.human_edge: Choose a decision worth supporting, negotiate definitions and prevent a polished tool from implying more certainty than the data supports.
tasks.pattern_why: A coding agent can draft a model, queries, output and tests across several steps. Business acceptance and production deployment remain human decisions.

in_practice.trigger: A request has an approved purpose, owner, audience and acceptance criteria.
steps: Create a specification covering measures, sources, lawful access and retention.
Generate alternative prototypes with synthetic data and select one with users.
Build the selected model and output in an isolated development environment.
Reconcile joins and totals, test cohort boundaries and attempt unauthorised access scenarios.
Present documentation, operating costs and test evidence for approval before release.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst and business owner approve definitions and acceptance; IT approves deployment and security, with privacy and OR review where applicable.
systems: Recruitee and Studytube validated exports or integrations
data_needed: Historical sample cases and expected results
in_practice.logs_to: Proposed version-controlled build history and SharePoint data-product register containing owner, approvals, tests and release version.

evidence.claim: AFAS documents API-based extraction for BI through GetConnectors; this does not establish availability of all required cross-system data.
Employment is a named high-risk area under the EU AI Act; intended use must be assessed before extending descriptive tools into AI hiring or worker-management decisions.
The gated development design is plausible; the 50% human-time saving and 1.8-times speedup are unmeasured.

risks: A technically correct join can associate a candidate with the wrong employee.
Automatically generated measures can mishandle rehires, multiple contracts or retrospective corrections.
A descriptive dashboard can drift into individual scoring or decision support requiring a separate AVG and EU AI Act assessment; human approval alone does not settle classification.
New tools can create more maintenance than one analyst can sustain.
research_questions: Which requested tools share enough definitions and joins to justify a reusable data product?
Are recruitment, training and employment histories available at the required granularity?
Can generated prototypes pass independent reconciliation and permission checks?
How much delivery time is coding versus requirements, access approval and source preparation?

tasks.short: Reconcile employee records and publish trusted hiring, movement and absence statistics.

today.trigger: Personnel changes arrive or a recurring workforce statistics report is due.
steps: Extract hires, transfers, contract changes, departures and permitted absence records.
Check effective dates, duplicates and missing organisational fields.
Compare discrepancies with source records and ask HR Administrators to resolve them.
Compile statistics using agreed employee, FTE and absence definitions.
Reconcile totals and publish to authorised audiences.
today.time_sinks: Effective-dated corrections and inconsistent employee, contract and agency-worker counts create repeated reconciliation.

lenses.faster: Apply automated checks for missing fields, conflicting dates and unexpected movements. Recalculate statistics from controlled snapshots rather than editing spreadsheets.
lenses.autonomous: After each extract, produce reconciled statistics and a separate exception queue. Routine reporting runs automatically; changes to personnel source records stay with authorised HR staff.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain consistent workforce history across all sites and distinguish employees from the seasonal agency workforce. Make the effect of retrospective corrections visible.
lenses.joy: Remove row-by-row comparisons and repeated arithmetic. Keep resolving ambiguous records and improving data quality with administrators.
lenses.options: Show headcount, FTE and agency hours separately, with reconciled views by site and applicable CAO. Avoid forcing unlike workforce measures into one total.
lenses.altitude: Own workforce data definitions and controls instead of repeatedly cleaning each report.
reach: HR Administrator preparation of personnel-data exception queues
Payroll Specialist pre-close checks of workforce movements
Controller reconciliation of staffing counts and labour-cost populations

tasks.human_edge: Interpret ambiguous contracts, CAO mappings and effective dates, and decide which source correction is justified.
tasks.pattern_why: Record validation, effective-date handling and statistical calculations are rules-based and auditable. Routine reporting does not require a language model.

in_practice.trigger: A new AFAS extract or approved agency-hours file becomes available.
steps: Load permitted fields and retain controlled snapshots under the agreed retention policy.
Check identifiers, effective dates, contract overlaps and organisational mappings.
Reconcile opening population plus movements to the closing population.
Generate statistics and route exceptions to the responsible HR Administrator.
Publish validated aggregates and record later corrections without silently replacing reported history.
in_practice.human_gate: HR Administrators approve source corrections; Payroll approves payroll-impacting changes, and the analyst approves definitions and unresolved reporting exceptions.
systems: Proposed scheduled validation and history job
data_needed: Employee and contract identifiers with effective dates
Site, department, contracted hours and applicable CAO mappings
Permitted administrative absence dates and percentages
Approved statistical definitions and historical reconciliation totals
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted data-quality register and versioned reporting snapshots; logs contain record references rather than copied personnel dossiers.

evidence.claim: AFAS supports controlled extraction through GetConnectors, providing a possible input to repeatable validation.
The Dutch data protection authority limits employers to necessary sickness information and excludes recording diagnoses or causes disclosed by employees.
The 70% human-time saving and 2.5-times speedup are estimates for record reconciliation and statistics, not for all personnel administration.

risks: Employment headcount, contract count, FTE and agency hours are different measures.
Historical employment and CAO mappings may be overwritten or incomplete.
Absence reporting must exclude diagnoses and medical notes and restrict access to necessary administrative data.
Statistical automation does not fulfil Wet verbetering poortwachter case-management duties; the responsible HR case owner remains accountable.
Savings overlap with report production unless record reconciliation and final reporting are measured separately.
research_questions: Does AFAS retain the effective-dated history needed to reconstruct past reporting periods?
Which source-record corrections can only HR Administration or Payroll authorise?
Are absence denominators and agency-worker treatment consistent across sites?
Can automated controls detect known historical errors without generating an unmanageable exception queue?

tasks.short: Explain how regional labour-market changes could affect hiring and retention at our three sites.

today.trigger: Recruitment slows, a workforce plan is reviewed, or a relevant labour-market publication appears.
steps: Collect dated regional labour-market information and applicable CAO updates.
Compare external definitions and geography with Noordhaven's role families and sites.
Review internal hiring, offer acceptance, retention and agency-use trends.
Develop possible explanations and workforce scenarios.
Brief HR leadership and site stakeholders on implications and uncertainty.
drudgery: Searching repeatedly for the latest publication
Extracting tables and checking publication dates
today.time_sinks: Reconciling different regions, occupation definitions and publication periods before a comparison is meaningful.

lenses.faster: Monitor approved sources and draft a dated, cited comparison with internal trends. Repeated searching and first-pass table extraction shrink.
lenses.autonomous: A new source release or agreed internal threshold triggers a draft briefing. The analyst validates comparability and interpretation before it is used.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain regional hiring and staffing scenarios for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo. Connect market conditions to the likely supply of productive, retained hires rather than vacancy volume alone.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive source collection and formatting. Keep the investigation of what the evidence means locally.
lenses.options: Compare recruitment, internal training, retention improvements and agency capacity under explicit assumptions. Show sensitivity ranges rather than one forecast.
lenses.altitude: Design a recurring workforce intelligence process instead of producing occasional research notes.
reach: Recruiter labour-market briefings
Compensation and Benefits preparation of market comparisons
FP&A workforce capacity and staffing-cost scenarios

tasks.human_edge: Judge whether regional evidence fits Noordhaven's shifts, qualifications and employment terms, and challenge convenient causal stories.
tasks.pattern_why: Research combines multiple sources, table extraction, internal comparisons and a written interpretation. An agent can prepare the evidence pack, but strategic conclusions need review.

in_practice.trigger: An approved external source publishes new data or an internal aggregate crosses an agreed threshold.
steps: Retrieve approved publications and record source links, release dates, reference periods and definitions.
Extract figures and flag incompatible geography, occupation categories or missing observations.
Compare compatible external data with approved aggregate internal measures.
Draft a cited briefing and alternative scenarios with visible assumptions and sensitivity ranges.
Have the analyst validate numerical claims and discuss implications with HR, Finance and site owners.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves every briefing; HR and Finance owners decide actions, with CAO checks and OR involvement where applicable.
data_needed: Regional vacancy and labour-supply indicators with reference periods
Approved CAO versions and pay assumptions
Aggregate time to hire, offer acceptance and mature 90-day outcomes
Agency hours, rates and capacity assumptions
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint labour-market evidence register with source snapshots, extracted figures, scenario assumptions and approved briefing versions.

evidence.claim: UWV's Regio in Beeld dashboard provides regional indicators and states scheduled updates for vacancy, labour-market tightness and registered-jobseeker figures.
An agent could compile cited evidence and scenario drafts, but regional comparability and strategic interpretation remain review tasks.
The 45% human-time saving and 1.7-times briefing speedup are untested estimates.

risks: Publication dates can be recent while the underlying observations are old.
Labour-market regions and occupation categories may not match the sites' actual recruitment catchments.
External trends and internal outcomes can move together without a causal connection.
Agency rate comparisons can omit shift premiums, qualifications or differences in service.
A model can misquote a CAO clause or invent a source; every numerical and contractual claim needs verification.
research_questions: Which external sources are comparable enough to support decisions for each site and role family?
Would historical scenario briefings have changed a real staffing or hiring decision?
Can extracted figures and citations be reproduced reliably across several publications?
Which assumptions about agency capacity, training lead times and retention most change the scenarios?

role.altitude: Become the owner of trusted HR information and workforce measurement: define outcomes, maintain reliable data products and help HR test improvements to productive 90-day hiring.
reach: Recruiter funnel measurement and labour-market briefings
HR Administrator data-quality controls and exception preparation
L&D onboarding and certificate outcome measurement
Payroll pre-close workforce reconciliation, with Payroll retaining sign-off
Controller workforce population and labour-cost reconciliation
FP&A workforce capacity scenarios using approved operational assumptions
role.ceiling_note: Current workflows and anatomy percentages are inferred from the brief. The listed tasks total 894.5 hours/year, about 55.9% of a 1,600-hour year. Estimated reductions imply about 606 gross human hours, worth roughly EUR 47,300 at EUR 78/hour, before implementation, upkeep, overlap and new demand; this is capacity value, not a cash saving. The other 705.5 hours are unassessed. All speedups estimate processing after required inputs are available and do not accelerate nightly feeds, external publications or human approvals. Gains depend on identifiers, recorded productivity milestones, licensing, IT support and independent review for a one-person function.
skills_to_grow: Effective-dated HR data modelling, SQL and Power BI measures
Version control, meaningful reconciliation tests and controlled releases
Cross-system identity matching and source ownership
Cohort measurement, uncertainty and practical evaluation of HR interventions
AVG data minimisation, access design, retention and disclosure controls
Working with the OR on applicable employee-data arrangements
Assessing intended AI use under the EU AI Act before introducing hiring or worker-management scoring
Managing coding and research agents with clear acceptance criteria
Explaining workforce evidence to site managers and Finance
role.ambitious_version: Run a shared hire-to-day-90 measurement service across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo. Join recruitment, employment and training records under approved controls, add a manager-recorded productivity milestone, and help Recruiters, HRBPs and L&D evaluate onboarding and retention changes. Keep calculations reproducible, show uncertainty and pending outcomes, and measure success by better productive, retained hiring outcomes rather than more dashboards.
